Title: [from] “All Roads Lead to Chaco Canyon”
Author: by Karen Gibson
Content: Engineers, astronomers, architects, masons, craftsmen, farmers, and tradesmen-the ancient Pueblo people were all these and more. And the cultural center of this amazing Puebloan civilization was Chaco Canyon, where all roads led for trading, ceremonies, and more.

Chaco is a long canyon in New Mexico's San Juan Basin. It features `text(thirteen)` large villages, each of which consists of `text(hundreds)` of rooms. The Pueblo people who lived there from `text(A.D. 800)` to `1150` are referred to as Chacoans.

The Chacoans built great houses on the canyon floor and on the mesas. The `text(first)` houses were built with mortar made of dirt and water. By the `text(eleventh century)`, the dwellings' inner walls were constructed with a core of rubble and facing wall stones. Sandstone was shaped and pieced together with small amounts of mortar for the outer walls.

Pueblo Bonito was `text(one)` of the `text(first)` of the great houses to be found. More than `600` rooms and `40` kivas¹ are in this `text(four-level)` dwelling. It is believed that the farming community at Pueblo Bonito probably understood and practiced astronomy. Evidence of this is the discovery of `text(two)` openings in Pueblo Bonito that were aligned to catch the sunlight on only `text(one day each year)` - the winter solstice. This suggests that the Chacoans understood solar (sun) and lunar (moon) changes.

Casa Rinconada, at the south side of Chaco Canyon, may have had a similar device to indicate the summer solstice. It also contained the largest known great kiva in Chaco, `text(one)` of the largest in the Southwest.

Pueblo del Arroyo, like Pueblo Bonito, was a D-shaped, multilevel, apartment-like house built in stages (`280` rooms and more than `20` kivas). A `text(three-wall)` structure, `text(one)` of only a few known in the Southwest, attached to the rear wall. `text(Each floor)` was made of layers of beams, poles, sticks, bark, and adobe. The beams have helped archaeologists put an age to the dwellings at Chaco Canyon. By examining the tree rings of the wood used, they can tell us what `text(year)` a dwelling was built... At Chaco, the last tree ring date is `text(A.D. 1132)`.

More than `text(four hundred miles)` of interlocking ancient roads have been discovered around Chaco Canyon. These are not simply worn pathways. Rather, they are roads as wide as `text(thirty feet)`, indicating the engineering knowledge of the Chacoans. The widest sections of the roads - `text(double)` and `text(quadruple)` segments - have been found closest to the Chaco Canyon great houses. Pueblo Alto, a great house built on top of a mesa, was the junction of several of these roads.

Chaco Canyon is a desert environment. Its lack of water would have made farming difficult. `text(One)` theory about Chaco is that the great houses were public houses. They may have been designed to manage and distribute the food supply as well as used for trading. `text(One)` piece of evidence leading to this theory is that excavations² at Pueblo Alto indicate that only `text(one)` in `text(twenty)` rooms showed signs of being used for human habitation.

A widespread trade network was almost certainly in place at Chaco Canyon. Many carved objects discovered at the Chetro Ketl site ... were made of materials from as far away as Mexico. The great amounts of turquoise found tell us that raw turquoise had been brought from distant mines... The distinctive black-on-white Cibola pottery excavated at Chaco may have been imported from areas beyond Chaco. Probably only `text(twenty percent)` of the pottery used at Chaco was made there.

By the `text(mid-1100s)`, there was a decline in the Chacoan population. A significant drought, which occurred sometime between `text(A.D. 1130)` and `1180`, may have driven the people to other areas. Overuse of the land and depletion³ of resources may have been other factors. It also is possible that warfare played a role, although no evidence of conflict has been discovered.

The ancient Pueblo people of Chaco Canyon organized, planned, and built amazing dwellings and roads. They also designed beautiful turquoise jewelry and objects, carved flutes, and made pottery. But for all the tangible things left by these ancient people, there is still much that is not known.
